title: Language models classify disempowerment patterns in real AI assistant conversations
summary: In a one-week sample of about 1.5 million Claude.ai conversations, severe disempowerment potential was rare (<1/1,000 overall) but higher in some personal domains; more disempowering interactions received higher user approval. Classifier predictions were compared with human labels; >95% fell within one severity level. The observational study is limited to Claude.ai and cannot establish user actions or generalization to other providers.
ai_technology: Prompted language models classify and summarize the conversation corpus; embeddings and k-means support privacy-preserving clustering to reveal recurring patterns.

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 submitted 2026-01-27. Methods classify 1,499,397 Claude consumer conversations using prompted language models, then use embeddings, k-means and privacy-preserving summaries; Results report severe disempowerment potential below 1/1,000 conversations, higher prevalence in some personal domains, and an association with higher user approval. Classifiers were compared with human labels, with >95% within one severity level. Caveats: one provider, observational data cannot establish actual user effects or causation, and authors caution against high-precision interpretation. No matching active/archive result was found.
